P01.title: P01: Apply Ivanti mitigations on vpn-gw-01 (Ivanti Connect Secure) to break VPN to domain controller path
P01.summary: A confirmed attack path starts at the internet-facing corporate VPN, vpn-gw-01 (Ivanti Connect Secure). It chains CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 to gain a shell on the appliance. From there, cached admin credentials work on the IT jump host jump-it-01, and that host's admin group has RDP rights on domain controller dc-01. The validation agent reached dc-01 with read-only rights. Fixing the VPN appliance, the first step, breaks the whole path.
P01.why_it_matters: Both CVEs are in the CISA KEV catalog with known ransomware campaign use. EPSS scores are 0.99984 and 0.99999, near the top of all scored vulnerabilities. The path ends at the domain controller, a crown jewel asset. Control of it would give an attacker control of corporate identity across the utility.
fix_steps: Network Engineering: on vpn-gw-01 (Ivanti Connect Secure), 'apply mitigations per vendor instructions' for CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887, using Ivanti's fixed release for this appliance version.

If mitigations or a fixed release are not available for this version, follow the KEV direction to 'discontinue use of the product' and take vpn-gw-01 off the internet until it can be fixed or replaced.

Because the validation reached a shell on the appliance, check vpn-gw-01 for compromise with Ivanti's integrity checking tool and review appliance logs before returning it to service. If any sign of compromise is found, factory reset the appliance and rebuild it on the fixed release.

Rotate every admin and service credential stored or cached on vpn-gw-01, and tell the Windows Server and Identity teams so they can remove reuse of those credentials on jump-it-01 and review jump host RDP rights on dc-01.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-01 is running an Ivanti Connect Secure release that the vendor lists as fixed for CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887.
Confirm Ivanti's integrity checking tool reports a clean result on vpn-gw-01 after the fix and that the old cached credentials no longer work anywhere.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P01 (Corporate VPN to the domain controller) and confirm it can no longer get past vpn-gw-01.
P01.exec_line: Our corporate VPN has flaws used in ransomware attacks that let outsiders reach our domain controller; we are patching it now.
P01.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P02.title: Patch or mitigate Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 to break path P02 to the domain controller
P02.summary: Validated path P02 starts at vpn-gw-02 (Remote access VPN for field offices, Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN), which is exposed to the internet and affected by CVE-2024-21762, an out-of-bound write that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run code. From that foothold the path reaches fs-02 through CVE-2021-34527 (Print Spooler) and then dc-01 using a cached domain admin logon. Fixing the VPN gateway entry point breaks the whole path.
P02.why_it_matters: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller and a crown jewel asset. Both CVEs on the path are in CISA KEV with known ransomware campaign use. EPSS scores are very high: 0.846 for CVE-2024-21762 (99.7th percentile) and 0.998 for CVE-2021-34527 (99.96th percentile). A compromise of the domain controller would give an attacker control of the corporate Windows environment.
fix_steps: Network Engineering: per the CISA KEV required action for CVE-2024-21762, "apply mitigations per vendor instructions" on vpn-gw-02 (Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN) by upgrading FortiOS to a fixed release listed in Fortinet's advisory.

If a fixed release cannot be applied right away, apply Fortinet's interim mitigation for the advisory, such as disabling SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02. KEV says to "discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable."

Because this flaw has known ransomware use, review vpn-gw-02 for signs of prior compromise before and after patching, including unexpected admin accounts, configuration changes and unusual logs. Escalate any findings to incident response.
Separately, notify the Windows Server team to patch CVE-2021-34527 on fs-02, and notify the Identity team to remove the cached domain admin logon from fs-02, as defense in depth.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-02 reports a FortiOS version at or above the fixed release in Fortinet's advisory for CVE-2024-21762, or that SSL-VPN is disabled if the interim mitigation was used.
Run an authenticated vulnerability scan of vpn-gw-02 and confirm CVE-2024-21762 is no longer reported.
Ask the security team to rerun the autonomous validation of path P02 and confirm the entry step at vpn-gw-02 now fails.
P02.exec_line: An internet-facing field office VPN flaw could let attackers reach our domain controller; patching the VPN gateway closes this path.
P02.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P03.title: P03: Patch Citrix NetScaler Gateway nsg-01 and kill all sessions to break the contractor path to the email server
P03.summary: Validation confirmed that the internet-facing contractor gateway nsg-01 (Citrix NetScaler Gateway) leaks session tokens through CVE-2023-4966, allowing a contractor session to be taken over. From that foothold the email server exch-01 (Microsoft Exchange Server) responded to the CVE-2022-41040 server-side request forgery check. Fixing nsg-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P03.why_it_matters: Both CVEs are in the CISA KEV catalog with known ransomware campaign use. EPSS scores are 0.99999 for CVE-2023-4966 and 0.99956 for CVE-2022-41040, near the top of all scored CVEs. The gateway is exposed to the internet and gives an attacker a working contractor session that reaches the corporate email server.
fix_steps: Upgrade Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 (Contractor gateway) to the fixed firmware build named in the Citrix advisory for CVE-2023-4966, applying the vendor mitigations as KEV requires.
After the upgrade, kill all active and persistent sessions on nsg-01 per vendor instructions, including ICA, PCoIP, AAA, RNAT and LB persistence sessions, so stolen tokens no longer work.

Check nsg-01 for signs of compromise: review authentication and session logs since before the patch for session reuse from unexpected IP addresses, and look for unknown accounts, configuration changes or files on the appliance.
If the fixed build cannot be applied, discontinue use of the gateway for contractor access until it can, as the KEV required action directs.
Notify Messaging of any suspicious contractor sessions found so they can review exch-01 activity and schedule the Exchange update for CVE-2022-41040.
verify_steps: Confirm the nsg-01 firmware version matches or exceeds the fixed build listed in the Citrix advisory for CVE-2023-4966.
Confirm the active session list on nsg-01 contains only sessions created after the patch and session termination.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P03 (Contractor gateway to the email server) and confirm it no longer succeeds at nsg-01.
P03.exec_line: Our contractor remote access gateway can leak logins that lead to the email server; patching it and resetting sessions closes this path.
P03.route_reason: The path ends at exch-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to Network Engineering as owner of the entry point nsg-01.

P04.title: P04: Patch GlobalProtect on plant edge firewall fw-edge-03 to cut the internet path to the plant data historian
P04.summary: The validation tool confirmed a three-step path from the internet to the plant data historian (hist-01). It starts with command injection on the GlobalProtect portal of the plant edge firewall fw-edge-03 (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS, CVE-2024-3400). From there, a local admin password shared between the firewall's management account and the IT to OT jump host (ot-jump-01) opened the jump host, and the jump host can log on to the historian. No commands were sent to the historian. Fixing the firewall, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P04.why_it_matters: CVE-2024-3400 is in the CISA KEV catalog with known ransomware campaign use. Its EPSS score is 0.99999, in the 100th percentile, so exploitation is near certain. It lets an unauthenticated attacker run commands as root on the firewall. This path then reaches two crown jewel assets in the OT DMZ, the IT to OT jump host and the plant data historian.
fix_steps: Upgrade PAN-OS on fw-edge-03 to the fixed release named in the Palo Alto Networks bulletin for CVE-2024-3400, following the KEV requirement to "apply mitigations per vendor instructions."

Until the upgrade is in place, "enable Threat Prevention IDs available from the vendor" for this vulnerability on the GlobalProtect portal and gateway interfaces of fw-edge-03, as the KEV entry directs.
Root command execution was confirmed on fw-edge-03, so check it for signs of compromise following the vendor bulletin's guidance before returning it to normal service.

Rotate the fw-edge-03 management account password to a unique value that is not used on any other system, including ot-jump-01, and coordinate with OT Engineering so the jump host's local admin password is also changed.
verify_steps: Confirm fw-edge-03 reports a PAN-OS version listed as fixed in the vendor bulletin, or that the Threat Prevention protection for this vulnerability is active on the GlobalProtect interfaces.
Confirm the fw-edge-03 management account password has been changed and no longer matches the local admin password on ot-jump-01.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of attack path P04 and confirm it no longer succeeds at the first step.
P04.exec_line: An internet-facing plant firewall flaw, widely used by ransomware groups, could let attackers reach our plant data historian; patching the firewall closes this path.
P04.route_reason: The path ends at hist-01, the plant data historian, which is marked as a crown jewel, and it also passes through the crown jewel jump host ot-jump-01.

P05.title: Patch Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 (Vendor file exchange) for CVE-2023-34362
P05.summary: Validated path P05 has one step: the internet-facing Vendor file exchange (mft-01), running Progress MOVEit Transfer, is exposed to SQL injection via CVE-2023-34362. The validation tool confirmed the injection works without logging in, but only read the version table. Fixing mft-01 closes the whole path.
P05.why_it_matters: CVE-2023-34362 has been in the CISA KEV catalog since 2023-06-02 and is marked as known to be used in ransomware campaigns. Its EPSS score is 0.99934 (99.97th percentile), so exploitation in the wild is near certain. An unauthenticated attacker could read, change or delete the MOVEit database and the vendor files it holds. That would expose data shared with outside parties.
fix_steps: Until the patch is in place, limit internet access to the MOVEit Transfer web interface on mft-01 to known vendor sources, or take it offline.
Apply updates per vendor instructions (CISA KEV required action): install the fixed Progress MOVEit Transfer release for your version line on mft-01.

Because this flaw has known ransomware use, follow Progress guidance to check mft-01 for signs of prior compromise before restoring access. Look for unexpected files in the web root, unknown accounts and unusual database or file download activity.
Rotate MOVEit service and database credentials and reset any accounts found to be suspicious, then restore normal internet access.
verify_steps: Confirm in the MOVEit Transfer admin console that mft-01 reports a version at or above the Progress fixed release for CVE-2023-34362.
Confirm the compromise review found no unknown accounts, unexpected web files or unexplained data transfers, and record the result in this ticket.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of path P05 against mft-01 and confirm the SQL injection no longer succeeds.
P05.exec_line: Our internet-facing vendor file exchange has a known, actively exploited flaw used by ransomware groups; patching it closes the exposure.
P05.route_reason: The path ends at mft-01, which is not marked crown_jewel, so it goes straight to the asset owner, Enterprise Applications.

P06.title: Patch CVE-2023-22515 on internet-facing Partner wiki (wiki-ext, Atlassian Confluence Data Center)
P06.summary: Validation confirmed that the Confluence setup endpoint on the Partner wiki (wiki-ext), which allows creating an administrator account, is reachable from the internet due to CVE-2023-22515. The agent stopped before creating an account. This single-step path gives an outside attacker full administrative control of the wiki.
P06.why_it_matters: CVE-2023-22515 is listed in CISA KEV with known ransomware campaign use, and its EPSS score is 0.9923 (99.9th percentile), meaning exploitation is very likely. wiki-ext sits directly on the internet and holds partner collaboration content, so a takeover would expose partner data and give attackers a foothold.
fix_steps: Apply the Atlassian-fixed Confluence Data Center version to wiki-ext per vendor instructions. If it cannot be patched right away, apply the vendor mitigations or take the Partner wiki offline, as KEV requires discontinuing use if mitigations are unavailable.
Until patching is complete, block internet access to the Confluence setup endpoints on wiki-ext at the reverse proxy or firewall, following Atlassian's mitigation guidance.

Check wiki-ext for evidence of compromise per vendor instructions, as KEV requires: review the confluence-administrators group for unexpected members, look for recently created accounts, and check for unknown plugins or changes.
If any unauthorized administrator accounts or other indicators are found, disable them, escalate to incident response, and report the positive findings to CISA as the KEV required action demands.
verify_steps: Confirm the Confluence version on wiki-ext is at or above the Atlassian fixed release for CVE-2023-22515.
From an external network, confirm the setup endpoints on the Partner wiki are no longer reachable.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P06 (Partner wiki takeover) and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P06.exec_line: Our internet-facing partner wiki has a widely exploited flaw allowing outsiders to become administrators; we are patching it and checking for intrusion.
P06.route_reason: The path ends at wiki-ext, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to the Collaboration Tools team.

P07.title: Patch ConnectWise ScreenConnect on rmm-01 to break the path to the virtualization cluster (P07)
P07.summary: Validated path P07 starts at rmm-01, the internet-facing ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote support console, where CVE-2024-1709 left the setup wizard reachable without authentication. From there the path reaches esxi-07, the VMware ESXi virtualization cluster, through CVE-2024-37085 because the hosts trust a directory group the support console can create. Fixing rmm-01 removes the entry point and breaks the whole path.
P07.why_it_matters: Both CVEs are in the CISA KEV catalog with known ransomware use. CVE-2024-1709 has an EPSS score of 0.99983 (99.98th percentile), so exploitation attempts are near certain. The console is exposed to the internet and leads to full control of the virtualization cluster, which can take down many hosted systems at once.
fix_steps: Apply the ConnectWise ScreenConnect mitigations per vendor instructions on rmm-01 by upgrading to the vendor's fixed release, as the KEV required action demands. If mitigations cannot be applied, discontinue use of the product or take rmm-01 offline.
Until the patch is in place, restrict access to the rmm-01 management interface so it is not reachable from the internet.

Check rmm-01 for compromise: review all ScreenConnect user accounts, remove any administrator accounts that were not created by IT Service Desk, and review session and audit logs for unexpected setup or login activity.

If any unknown accounts or sessions are found, end all active ScreenConnect sessions, reset administrator credentials, and escalate to the security team for incident response, including a check of directory groups trusted by esxi-07.
verify_steps: Confirm rmm-01 reports the vendor's fixed ScreenConnect version and that the setup wizard is no longer reachable without authentication.
Confirm the ScreenConnect administrator account list on rmm-01 contains only approved accounts.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P07 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P07.exec_line: An internet-facing remote support tool could let attackers take over our virtualization cluster; IT Service Desk is patching it now.
P07.route_reason: The path ends at esxi-07, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes directly to the IT Service Desk as owner of the fix point rmm-01.

P08.title: Remove internet exposure of Cisco IOS XE Web UI on substation router rtr-sub-12 (CVE-2023-20198)
P08.summary: Validated path P08 starts at rtr-sub-12, the Substation comms router running Cisco IOS XE, whose Web UI is reachable from the internet on a version affected by CVE-2023-20198. From there, a route with no access list reaches ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link. Fixing the router breaks the whole path.
P08.why_it_matters: CVE-2023-20198 is on the CISA KEV list and has an EPSS score of 0.998, among the highest of all scored vulnerabilities. It lets an unauthenticated remote attacker take full control of the router. From the router, the path reaches the EMS data link, a crown jewel asset for grid operations. No traffic was sent to the EMS link during validation.
fix_steps: Field Telecom: Verify that the Cisco IOS XE Web UI on rtr-sub-12 complies with BOD 23-02. Disable the Web UI, or restrict it so it is not reachable from the internet or other untrusted networks.
Apply Cisco's mitigations and the fixed IOS XE software release for CVE-2023-20198 on rtr-sub-12, following vendor instructions.

Because the Web UI was exposed to the internet, follow Cisco's instructions to determine whether rtr-sub-12 may have been compromised. Check for unknown local accounts and unauthorized configuration or implant indicators.
Immediately report any positive compromise findings to CISA and to the security team. If compromise is found, treat ems-link-01 as potentially exposed.
Coordinate with Grid Operations to add an access list between the substation comms network and the EMS data link as follow-up hardening.
verify_steps: Confirm from an external vantage point that the rtr-sub-12 Web UI is no longer reachable from the internet.
Confirm that rtr-sub-12 runs a Cisco IOS XE release fixed for CVE-2023-20198 and that Cisco's compromise checks came back clean.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of path P08 and confirm it is broken at rtr-sub-12.
P08.exec_line: An internet-exposed substation router with a widely exploited flaw could give attackers a route to our energy management system; we are closing it.
P08.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, which is marked crown_jewel.

P09.title: Patch Apache Log4j2 on Outage map API (outage-api) to break path P09
P09.summary: Validated path P09 shows the internet-facing Outage map API (outage-api), a Java service using Apache Log4j2, is exposed to CVE-2021-44228. A harmless test string in a request header caused the service to make an outbound DNS query, confirming the vulnerable lookup behavior is reachable from the internet. This is a single-step path, so fixing outage-api breaks it entirely.
P09.why_it_matters: CVE-2021-44228 is in the CISA KEV catalog with known ransomware campaign use, and its EPSS score is 0.99999 (100th percentile), meaning exploitation attempts are near certain. The asset sits in the internet zone and allows remote code execution, giving an attacker a foothold on utility infrastructure.
fix_steps: Customer Applications: identify every Apache Log4j2 library bundled with the Outage map API (outage-api), including nested or shaded copies inside dependencies.

Apply updates: upgrade Apache Log4j2 to a fixed, currently supported release, rebuild and redeploy outage-api. Per CISA KEV, applying updates or removing the asset from the network are the only acceptable remediations.

If the update cannot be deployed immediately, apply a CISA ED 22-02 recommended temporary mitigation or take outage-api offline; temporary mitigations are only acceptable until the update is in place.

Check outage-api for signs of prior compromise: review logs for past lookup strings in requests, unexpected outbound DNS or network connections, and unknown files or processes, and escalate to incident response if anything is found.
verify_steps: Confirm the deployed outage-api build contains only the fixed Apache Log4j2 version and no older Log4j2 copies remain in the artifact.
Confirm outage-api no longer makes unexpected outbound DNS or network connections, and restrict its outbound traffic to required destinations only.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P09 to confirm the outage map API is no longer exploitable.
P09.exec_line: Our public outage map service has a widely exploited flaw allowing remote takeover; the application team will patch it and check for intrusion.
P09.route_reason: The path ends at outage-api, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes directly to the Customer Applications team.

P10.title: Patch and restrict Fortinet FortiManager fmgr-01 device registration exposure (CVE-2024-47575)
P10.summary: Validated path P10 shows the Firewall manager (fmgr-01, Fortinet FortiManager) runs a version affected by CVE-2024-47575, a missing authentication flaw in the fgfmd daemon. Its device registration port answered from the corporate user network. This is a single-step path, so fixing fmgr-01 breaks it.
P10.why_it_matters: CVE-2024-47575 is listed in CISA KEV, and its EPSS score of 0.948 (99.9th percentile) means exploitation is very likely. The flaw lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run code on the system that manages the firewalls. Control of fmgr-01 could expose firewall configurations and credentials and allow changes to firewall policy across the utility's network.
fix_steps: Network Engineering: apply mitigations per Fortinet's instructions for CVE-2024-47575 on FortiManager fmgr-01, upgrading to a fixed release. KEV requires discontinuing use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
Until the upgrade is done, apply Fortinet's interim mitigations. Block unknown devices from registering, and restrict which source addresses can reach the device registration port.
Restrict network access so the fmgr-01 device registration port is reachable only from managed FortiGate devices, not from the corporate user network.

Check fmgr-01 for signs of compromise using Fortinet's published indicators: unknown registered devices, unexpected files, and unexpected outbound connections. If any are found, escalate to incident response and rotate credentials for the managed FortiGates.
verify_steps: Confirm fmgr-01 reports a FortiManager version that Fortinet lists as fixed for CVE-2024-47575.
From a host on the corporate user network, confirm the fmgr-01 device registration port no longer answers.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P10 to confirm it is broken.
P10.exec_line: A severe, actively exploited flaw in our firewall management system is reachable from the office network and needs patching and access restriction now.
P10.route_reason: The path ends at fmgr-01, which is not marked crown_jewel, so the ticket goes directly to Network Engineering.

P11.title: Patch Netlogon (Zerologon) on domain controller dc-01
P11.summary: Validation confirmed that domain controller dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory) accepted a vulnerable Netlogon secure channel from a corporate workstation, exposing it to CVE-2020-1472. The agent stopped before changing any password. This single-step path reaches a crown jewel asset directly from the corporate network.
P11.why_it_matters: CVE-2020-1472 is in the CISA KEV catalog with known ransomware campaign use, and its EPSS score is 0.99389 (99.9th percentile). A successful attack on dc-01 could give an attacker control of Active Directory and with it the whole corporate domain.
fix_steps: Apply the Microsoft security updates for CVE-2020-1472 to dc-01 and every other domain controller in the domain, per the KEV required action: "Apply updates per vendor instructions."
Follow Microsoft's guidance to enable Netlogon secure channel enforcement mode on all domain controllers so vulnerable connections are rejected.
Review the domain controller event logs for Netlogon events that show denied or vulnerable secure channel connections, and fix or retire any devices still using them.
Check dc-01 for signs of compromise, such as unexpected changes to the domain controller machine account password, and escalate any findings to incident response.
verify_steps: Confirm that dc-01 and all other domain controllers report the vendor update for CVE-2020-1472 as installed.
Confirm that the Netlogon enforcement setting is active on dc-01 and that the event logs show vulnerable secure channel attempts being denied.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of path P11 and confirm that dc-01 no longer accepts a vulnerable Netlogon secure channel.
P11.exec_line: Our main domain controller has a widely exploited flaw that could let an attacker take over the corporate network; patching it closes this.
P11.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, which is marked as a crown jewel asset, so the ticket needs human review before assignment.

P12.title: Restrict RDP and require MFA on OT jump host ot-jump-01 to block corporate access to EMS data link
P12.summary: Validated path P12 runs from the corporate network to the energy management system data link (ems-link-01) through the IT to OT jump host (ot-jump-01). The jump host, running Microsoft Windows Server, accepts RDP from the entire corporate network with password-only sign-in and no multi-factor prompt. The EMS data link then trusts logons coming from that jump host. The validation agent reached the RDP logon prompt from a corporate desktop VLAN but did not attempt a logon. No CVEs are involved; this is a misconfiguration.
P12.why_it_matters: Both assets are crown jewels. Anyone holding or guessing a single corporate password could reach the jump host and, through the trust relationship, the EMS data link that supports grid operations. Restricting and hardening access at the jump host closes the path at its entry point.
fix_steps: On ot-jump-01 (Microsoft Windows Server), limit inbound RDP at the host firewall and the IT/OT boundary firewall to an approved list of administrator workstations or a dedicated privileged access network, removing access from the general corporate network and desktop VLANs.
Require multi-factor authentication for all RDP sign-ins to ot-jump-01, for example through an RD Gateway or MFA provider, and disallow password-only sign-in.
Review the local and domain groups allowed to log on through Remote Desktop on ot-jump-01 and remove any accounts that do not need OT access.
Review recent RDP logon events on ot-jump-01 for unexpected sources or accounts and escalate anything unexplained to the security team.
verify_steps: From a standard corporate desktop VLAN, confirm the RDP service on ot-jump-01 is no longer reachable.
From an approved administrator workstation, confirm an RDP sign-in to ot-jump-01 prompts for a second factor and fails with a password alone.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P12 to confirm it is broken.
P12.exec_line: Any corporate user's password could reach the grid energy management link; we are restricting and adding multi-factor sign-in to the gateway server.
P12.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, which is marked as a crown jewel, and changes to the OT jump host affect operational access to grid systems.
